comments.author: losvedir
comments.story_title: Steps to Anonymous and Secured Communication
comments.why_zh: 解释了 OTR 相对于 PGP 签名所具有的否认性优势
comments.quote_zh: 至少，这是我从那段精彩视频[1]里领会到的
comments.text_zh: > 或者，也许可以用不带日志记录的 OTR 即时通讯，但那……也可能栽在疯狂的对方手上——对方要么不关闭日志记录，要么故意录音并以此敲诈。我原以为这正是 OTR 相对于比如 PGP 的优点之一。也就是说，用 PGP 时，如果你对一条消息签名，对方可以拿着它到处挥舞说“看看这人说了什么”，而用 OTR 时，由于加密用的是共享密钥，同样有可能是对方自己编造出来的。至少，这是我从昨天某人在 HN 上链接的那段精彩视频[1]里领会到的。[1] [视频]
comments.text: > Or, maybe, IM with OTR without logging, but that . . . might also fall prey to crazy counterparty either not disabling logging or intentionally recording and blackmailing. I thought this was one of the benefits of OTR over, say, PGP. That is, with PGP if you sign a message the counterparty can wave it around and say "look at what this poerson said", while with OTR, since the encryption is done with a shared key, it could be just as likely that the counterparty made it up. At least, that's what I gleaned from this wonderful video[1] someone linked to on HN yesterday. [1] [VIDEO]

comments.author: CodeMage
comments.why_zh: 说明技术如何重塑社会，因此拒绝参与是有代价的
comments.quote_zh: 我绝对建议完整观看，但其中的关键要点
comments.text_zh: > 我认为 HN 上意见色彩的差异，部分与透明度有些关系。并不是说我在透明度这个话题上不同意你，而是说，我认为我们不能把两个非常不同的话题上的观点拿来比较，仿佛它们是同一个话题。抱怨订阅内容提供商太多的人，实际上并不是在支持或反对垄断。那不是同一场讨论。 > 而我会说，Google 和 Facebook 在主动告知公众方面做得还不够：它们收集了什么、如何借此创收，以及目前存储了用户的哪些信息。我承认这一点，但我很确定，即使它们这么做了，也不会有多大区别。我总是让人们去看 Moxie Marlinspike 在 DEF CON 上的主题演讲，题为“Changing threats to privacy”[1]。我绝对建议完整观看，但就这次讨论而言，它的关键要点是：归根结底在于选择。他谈到技术如何改变社会结构，如何改变人们互动、沟通和协作的方式，而拒绝参与这种新的做事方式会让你承受“no network effect”。这就是为什么 Google 和 Facebook 仅仅告知人们它们收集什么、如何使用，是不够的。只要它们实际上处于垄断地位，它们就可以披露和告知，然后照旧行事，因为没有其他可行的替代选择，而且它们会努力确保
comments.text: > I think part of the difference in HN opinion color is somewhat related to transparency. It's not that I disagree with you on the topic of transparency, it's that I think we can't really compare opinions on two very different topics as if they were the same topic. People complaining about too many subscription content providers are not really arguing for or against a monopoly. It's not the same discussion. > And I'd say Google and Facebook haven't done a sufficient job in proactively informing the public about what they collect, how they generate revenue from it, and what's currently stored about a user. Granted, but I'm pretty sure that even if they did so, it wouldn't make much difference. I always refer people to Moxie Marlinspike's DEF CON keynote called "Changing threats to privacy" [1]. I would definitely recommend watching it in full, but the key takeaway from it -- for the purposes of this discussion -- is that it all boils down to choice. He talks about the way technology changes the fabric of the society, how it changes the way people interact, communicate and coordinate, and declining to participate in this new way of doing things exposes you to the "no network effect". This is why it's not enough for Google and Facebook to merely inform people about what they collect and how they use it. As long as they're practically monopolies, they can disclose and inform and then go on just the same, because there's no other viable alternative and they'll work hard to ensure

comments.author: jiggy2011
comments.story_title: I Don't Want To Be Part of Your Ecosystem
comments.why_zh: 阐述了为什么在达到临界规模后追踪很难摆脱
comments.text_zh: 很多人同样不在乎参加选举投票、捐钱做慈善、参与公众示威，或者照顾自己的健康。问题并不在于人们是否介意自己的位置被追踪，或者是否对自己的硬件有控制权等等。更关键的是，一旦这些东西达到临界规模，如果我们不喜欢现状，就很难再回头；对个人来说，也很难选择一种置身于这些东西之外的生活。这里讲得很清楚：[视频] 大约 09:00 处
comments.text: Lots of people don't care about voting in elections, giving to charity, partaking in public demonstrations or looking after their health either. The problem is not so much whether people mind if their location is tracked or whether they have control over their hardware etc. It's more that once these things reach a critical mass it is very difficult to start to go back if we don't like where we are or indeed for an individual to make a choice to live outside of this stuff. It is articulated quite well here: [VIDEO] At around 09:00

comments.author: throa8923489
comments.why_zh: Moxie 关于法西斯主义与社会民主主义的框架被用到了 Glass 上
comments.quote_zh: 我们以为会迎来法西斯主义，结果却迎来了社会民主主义。
comments.text_zh: 这让我想起 moxie 的这个演讲 [VIDEO]。我们以为会迎来法西斯主义，结果却迎来了社会民主主义。不过，我们能够通过适当的法律来应对这件事。欧洲肯定会走这条路，美国大概也会跟上。比如，用摄像头拍摄并存储或分享照片/视频（而不是只由某些增强现实算法处理），就可以要求在眼镜框上装一盏小灯。就像录像机一样，但没法（轻易地！）把它关掉。
comments.text: Reminds me of this talk [VIDEO] by moxie. We thought we would get facism, instead we got social democracy. We will be able to deal with this, though, using appropriate laws. Europe will certainly go down that route, the US will probably follow. For example, using the camera to take pictures or videos that are stored or shared (vs. just processed by some augmented reality algorithms) could enable a small lamp on the frame of the glasses. Just like a video recorder, but without the ability to (easily!) turn it off.

comments.text_zh: 重点是，Google 并不只是在“卖广告位”。他们收集关于你的数据，而且自己都承认宁愿永远不删除任何东西。关键词是“定向投放”，还记得吗？在这个过程中，他们对你的了解仍然比你母亲或伴侣还多。在他们内部的某个地方，存着一堆关于你的数据，其深度在以前甚至难以想象。我们是怎么走到这一步的：Moxie Marlinspike，2010：[VIDEO]

In process, they still know more about you than your mother or partner. Somewhere in their guts, there is a collection of data about you, the depth of it not even imaginable before. How we got here: Moxie Marlinspike, 2010: [VIDEO]
